newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia stocks seen staying strong in '97.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia stocks seen staying strong in '97.

text.p: Malaysian stocks will continue to be strong in 1997, in spite of recent falls on the key index led by market heavyweights Tenaga Nasional Bhd and Telekom Malaysia Bhd, analysts said.
And some analysts forecast the main index would reach new highs this year.
"Fundamentally, the market has not changed. I still see the market hitting 1,360 by the year's end," Ramlan Ahmad, senior manager at fund manager Commerce MGI Sdn Bhd, said on Wednesday.
The benchmark Composite Index was down 7.93 points at 1,220.96 at the midday close on Wednesday, dented by profit-taking in blue-chip stocks.
The index's all-time high of 1,332.04 was set in January 1994.

The share prices of blue-chip utility Tenaga and telecommunications firm Telekom were both recently hit by speculation that their dominance of their respective markets would be broken by deregulation.

Local newspaper reports on Tuesday said the government had awarded licences to a consortium of companies to generate, distribute and sell electricity to firms operating in an industrial park in the northern Malaysian state of Kedah.
Some saw this as the beginning of the end of Tenaga's monopoly of the electricity distribution system in the country.

Meanwhile sentiment on Telekom turned bearish when Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie said on Monday that he would welcome deregulation within that industry sooner, rather than later. Telekom and Tenaga are major contributors to the movement of the Composite Index, which is a weighted average of 100 stocks.
"Tenaga is way off its high, but fundamentally it's still expensive," said Ramlan. "Tenaga must improve by two to three dollars if the Composite Index is going to be strong".
But the overall market's underlying trend remains bullish, said analysts.

"The primary bull trend at this juncture is still fundamentally intact," said the Malaysian Investors' Association (MIA) in a report released on Wednesday on the outlook for the Malaysian market in 1997.
The MIA forecast the main index would hit 1,350 this year.
The performance of the U.S. bourse would be watched closely, as it would have an impact on the local market, said analysts.
They expect a correction for the U.S. markets in the wake of last year's bull run, which boosted the key Dow Jones Industrial Average to record highs.

"A serious and meaningful correction, if any, in Wall Street could, in the end, benefit other stock markets outside America. The U.S. stock markets over the past two years had been sponging vast global pension and investment funds, leaving very little for funds for the Asian markets," said the MIA.

"As long as companies provide profits, the market will go up," Seacorp-Schroder Capital Management's general manager John Ford said, adding that Malaysia's political stability should also provide support.
Seacorp-Schroder's projection for the Composite Index was particularly bullish.
"It's 1,450...we were right about last year being 1,250," Ford said.
And corporate earnings would continue to be firm in 1997, said analysts.
"Corporate earnings for 1997 are expected to improve by a moderate rate of 18 to 20 percent," said the MIA.
Analysts said the prospective market price-to-earnings ratio was around 25 times for 1997.
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-201 4813)
